title: Working with standards at MOSCATELLI
summary: A demonstration reference for how standards should guide decisions without turning judgement into bureaucracy.
contentNotice: Demonstration content for Atlas interface development; not final MOSCATELLI policy.

blocks.text: Standards create a shared quality threshold and a repeatable point of reference. They should support judgement rather than replace it.

blocks.label: Principle
blocks.text: A standard should make an important decision clearer. If it only creates paperwork without protecting quality, consistency or accountability, it should be reconsidered.
Use a published standard when the work falls within its stated scope. If circumstances materially differ, record the exception rather than silently ignoring the standard.

items: Confirm that the current version applies
Identify any material exception before proceeding
Record who approved a departure when one is necessary
Feed recurring exceptions back into the next review

blocks.text: Luxury quality depends on discernment as well as consistency. A standard defines the floor and the shared vocabulary; creative and commercial judgement still determine the best answer within that framework.
